layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
layers.process: Assam is not listed in the Third (Protected Areas) or Fourth (Restricted Areas) Schedule of the Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025, so no state-wide Protected or Restricted Area Permit applies. e-Visa holders can enter India at Guwahati airport and the Darranga land port (MHA list of 10 August 2026).

sources.title: Immigration and Foreigners Order, 2025 (S.O. 3986(E), 1 September 2025)
sources.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (Gazette of India copy hosted by the High Court of Tripura)
sources.supports: paragraph 14 (permit to enter or stay, e-FRRO or Su-Swagatam application, electronic permit, civil authority conditions incl. photography); Third Schedule (Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim entire state); Fourth Schedule (no Assam, Meghalaya or Tripura entries) (read directly)

sources.title: List of international ports enabling entry of e-Visa holders (10 August 2026)
sources.authority: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.supports: 88 e-Visa entry points; airports include Bagdogra and Guwahati; land ports include Jaigaon, Darranga, Dawki, Agartala and Moreh (newly added) (read directly)

zone-requirements.note: Permits for neighbouring states (Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram) are needed before crossing into them. Prohibited places under the Official Secrets Act still need permission.

laws.rule: Assam Tourism’s Kaziranga brochure states that a Forest Department guide must accompany tourists in Kaziranga National Park. The brochure is older; confirm the current arrangement with the park.
laws.heading: Kaziranga National Park visitor brochure

laws.rule: Assam Tourism’s forest etiquette guidance asks safari visitors to use an authorised park or sanctuary guide, stay on specified routes, leave before sunset and not get out of the vehicle; confirm current conditions with the particular park.
laws.heading: Assam Tourism coffee-table book: Forest Etiquette

laws.rule: Assam Tourism’s forest etiquette guidance says safari visitors should not smoke or light fires. Confirm the current rule at the particular park or sanctuary.
laws.heading: Assam Tourism coffee-table book: Forest Etiquette

laws.rule: Assam Tourism’s forest etiquette guidance asks safari visitors not to bring pets or throw litter. Confirm the current rule at the particular park or sanctuary.

laws.rule: Assam Tourism’s forest etiquette guidance says safari visitors should not use musical instruments, horns, whistles or mobile phones. Confirm current conditions with the particular park or sanctuary.
